title: A half-center oscillator regulates sleep pressure
title_zh: 半中心振荡器调节睡眠压力
abstract: Abstract Changes in oscillatory neural dynamics reflect—but may not necessarily determine—transitions between sleep stages and variations in sleep pressure. Here we show that sleep-control neurons innervating the dorsal fan-shaped body of Drosophila (dFBNs) produce slow-wave activity (SWA) that is causally linked to sleep. The dFBN ensemble contains bistable cells whose membrane voltages oscillate between hyperpolarized DOWN and depolarized UP states. The oscillations rely on interhemispheric competition of two half-centers connected by inhibitory glutamatergic synapses. dFBN-restricted interference with glutamate release disrupts SWA and baseline as well as rebound sleep, whereas the optogenetic replay of SWA induces sleep. dFBNs generate SWA throughout the sleep–wake cycle (despite mutual antagonism with arousing dopaminergic neurons) and adjust its power to sleep need via sleep history-dependent increases in excitability and homeostatic synaptic depression. The oscillatory format permits a continuous encoding of sleep pressure but requires mechanisms that convert the amplitude-modulated signal into binary sleep–wake states.
abstract_zh: 摘要：振荡神经动力学的变化反映了——但不一定决定——睡眠阶段之间的转换和睡眠压力的变化。我们在此展示，果蝇背侧扇形体（dFBN）的睡眠调控神经元产生慢波活动（SWA），并与睡眠具有因果关联。dFBN 集合包含双稳态细胞，其膜电位在超极化的 DOWN 状态和去极化的 UP 状态之间振荡。振荡依赖于由抑制性谷氨酸能突触连接的两半中心之间的脑半球竞争。限制 dFBN 释放谷氨酸的干预会破坏 SWA 以及基线和反弹睡眠，而光遗传学重放 SWA 则能诱导睡眠。dFBN 在睡眠-觉醒周期中持续产生 SWA（尽管与唤醒性多巴胺能神经元相互拮抗），并通过睡眠历史相关的兴奋性增加和稳态突触抑制来调节其功率以满足睡眠需求。振荡格式允许对睡眠压力进行连续编码，但需要将幅度调制信号转换为二进制睡眠-觉醒状态的机制。
